summary: Rose Bay Seaplane Base (RSE) is a heritage waterfront terminal in Sydney's affluent eastern suburb of Rose Bay, serving as the primary hub for seaplane operations on Sydney Harbour. The base has a rich aviation history dating back to the 1930s when it functioned as a major flying boat and seaplane terminal. Today, it is best known as the home of Sydney Seaplanes, offering scenic harbour flights and scheduled services to destinations along the NSW coastline.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Rose Bay Seaplane Base?
A: Sydney Seaplanes is the primary operator, offering scenic flights over Sydney Harbour and charter services to coastal destinations including Palm Beach, the Central Coast, and Port Stephens.

Q: Can you take a scenic flight from Rose Bay?
A: Yes, scenic flights over Sydney Harbour are one of the base's most popular offerings, typically lasting 15 to 30 minutes and providing aerial views of the Opera House, Harbour Bridge, and surrounding beaches.

Q: Is Rose Bay Seaplane Base connected to public transport?
A: The base is accessible by Sydney Ferries, with a wharf located nearby, as well as by bus services along New South Head Road. Ferry connections run regularly to Circular Quay in the CBD.

Q: Does the base handle international or large commercial flights?
A: No, Rose Bay exclusively handles small seaplane aircraft and does not accommodate large commercial jets. It is a general aviation and tourism-focused facility.
transport_tips: The most scenic way to reach Rose Bay Seaplane Base is by Sydney Ferry from Circular Quay, with services taking approximately 25 minutes and offering harbour views along the way. Bus route 323, 324, or 325 from the CBD stop near the terminal along New South Head Road. Driving is possible but parking in Rose Bay can be limited and time-restricted, so arriving by ferry or rideshare is often more convenient.
local_tip: Arrive at least 30 minutes before your flight to enjoy a coffee at one of the waterfront cafes overlooking the seaplane ramp — it is one of the best spots in Sydney to watch the seaplanes take off and land against the backdrop of the harbour.
